ov: The largest wild member of the dog family. Wolves live in family packs, usually a breeding pair and their young, that hunt large prey together over big territories.

why.dg: Attacks on people are rare, and most recorded ones involved wolves with rabies.
why.dm: Wolves were never domesticated. Dogs come from an ancient wolf population, and today’s wolves are a sister line, not dogs’ direct ancestors.
why.ac: Nocturnal hunters; in winter a pack starts hunting in the early-evening twilight.

wt: About 25–40 kg on average, by region
rg: Across much of North America, Europe and Asia, from Arctic tundra to forest, steppe and desert edges.
df: Mostly large hoofed animals such as deer, elk and moose, taken by the pack, plus smaller prey and carrion.

cf.tip: A wolf has longer legs, bigger feet, a broader head and a straight tail carried low. Many dogs carry their tails curled or high.
